guideSummary.surfForecast: Pacifico in Siargao Islands is an exposed reef break that has consistent surf. Autumn and winter are the best times of year for waves. The best wind direction is from the southwest. Waves more likely to be from local windswells than distant groundswells and the ideal wave direction is from the northeast. A left hand reef. It very rarely gets crowded here. Submerged rocks are a hazard.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Pansukian is a right-hand reef break facing the plush resort of the same name, and it was one of the original waves ridden on Siargao. It peels over a live coral shelf and can serve up some challenging sections when it lines up. Neighbouring Daku shelters it from northeast swell, so the setup relies on swell wrapping in from the east.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Quicksilver is Cloud 9's neighbouring reef peak, and it usually breaks at the same time as its more famous neighbour, just a touch smaller. The wave works over live coral, throwing a short, fast, hollow section off the peak before opening into a workable wall that runs down to a clean, defined channel. It favours the rights but has both lefts and rights on offer.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Stimpy's is a left-hand reef break over live coral, and on overhead swells it turns into a ferocious, unpredictable barrel that wraps around the coral heads with board-breaking power. On smaller days it settles into mushy, fun walls and shoulders. It's very much an expert wave, but it's consistent enough that there's usually something to ride.
guideSummary.surfForecast: Stimpy's in Siargao Islands is an exposed reef break that has reliable surf. Autumn and winter are the optimum times of year for waves. Offshore winds blow from the west southwest. Windswells are much more common than groundswells and the ideal wave direction is from the northeast. A reef breaks left. Good surf at all stages of the tide. Unlikely to be too crowded, even when the surf is up. Beware of locals and rocks.
